Checked source 3f94bc936c5d4a14 §1, equations (1)–(4), against its declared digest. The source restricts the nonempty null contact conclusion to destinations of zero residual.

Minkowski inclusion of endpoint fibers yields positive d-volume at all segment parameters. A strict point generates a positive-volume residual by taking small convex mixtures with an interior ball. Strict points at zero persist to small positive t by affine-margin interpolation with any destination point.

Strict-negative feasibility has an interval of parameters by convexity. Compactness gives a limiting closed residual point at its supremum. A strict point there for t<1 would extend the interval by mixing with a destination point; the t=1 case is excluded by the zero-residual hypothesis. The closed residual at the exit is therefore a nonempty subset of a null continuous hyperplane.

Reweighted displacement is exactly the original displacement divided by c, so it vanishes, and the weights sum to one. Closed residual sections have the same volumes as the strict ones and their weighted Minkowski sum lies in the closed residual at p. Brunn–Minkowski extends to the nonempty lower-dimensional contacts by adding a vanishing radius ball to each compact section.

The terms at the exits vanish, and t=1 for the other atoms, giving the desired inequality and exact algebraic correction factor, including the no-exits case c=1 and the possible zero-residual endpoint contact at t=1.

issues.exact_defect: Following both cases for j, the sentence reads as assigning zero volume to C_(b_j)∩{ℓ≤0} for every destination. If f(z_j)>0 then b_j=z_j and the volume is f(z_j)^d>0. For example use d=1, C=[−1,1]×[0,1], H={x≥1/2}, and the single atom p=z_1=0.
